decisive_items: Investigation of medical records revealed a history of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks prior to the development of the current eruption at the same site
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band in a polyclonal background
response.rationale: The eruption arose at a prior HSV-2 site and lacked a reproducible T-cell clone, favoring a reactive pseudolymphoma over a clonal T-cell lymphoma; the atypical CD4+ infiltrate with eosinophils/plasma cells is a known mimic.

rejected.why: Broad T-cell lymphoma is contradicted by absent reproducible clonality and the HSV-2-associated reactive context.
Dermatitis is unsupported by the dense atypical CD4+ infiltrate and epidermotropism on repeat biopsy.
Lymphomatoid papulosis typically shows CD30+ large atypical cells and recurrent self-healing papules, not persistent plaques/nodules.
Granuloma faciale is usually facial and lacks atypical CD4+ small/medium lymphocytic infiltrate.
Infectious dermatitis is not supported; syphilis was negative and no active HSV lesion is described.
Generic lymphoma is less specific and similarly contradicted by the non-reproducible clonal band.
Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma is a close mimic but is less likely given the HSV-2 trigger and lack of persistent clonal rearrangement.
